Web design Sarasota Florida businesses need starts with one plain fact about the people reading it. In Sarasota County, a large share of customers are retirees, and plenty of them are reading your site on a phone with the text size turned up. If your page breaks when that happens, or hides the phone number in a pale gray footer, you lose the very customer with the time and the money to come in.

Dominion Web Design Pro is Maurice Johnson. He writes every page himself, shows you a free demo of your own site before you spend a dollar, and charges one printed price.

Web design Sarasota Florida needs when more than a third of the county is over 65

Census Bureau estimates reported by Sarasota Magazine put 38.8% of Sarasota County residents at 65 or older in 2025. Inside the city limits the share is lower, 29.3% in the Census Bureau's QuickFacts figures, but the county is where most of your customers live.

None of that means old-fashioned design. It means design that does not make anyone work. Here is how that turns into choices on the page:

What a reader needsHow the page handles it
Text that is readable without zoomingLarge body type, short lines, dark text on a white background, no thin decorative fonts for anything important.
A clear way to reach youThe phone number at the top of every page, written out and tappable, plus a button that says "Call" in words.
Confidence about where you areYour street address, the nearest landmark road, and parking notes written in plain sentences.
No surprisesNo pop-ups covering the page, no auto-playing video, no menus that only open on hover.
Room for a bigger text settingLayouts that reflow when someone turns up the phone's font size, instead of overlapping or cutting words off.

How we check a Sarasota page before you see it

  1. Read it on a small phoneEvery page gets looked at on a narrow screen first, because that is where small type and crowded buttons show up.
  2. Turn the text size upWe enlarge the font and make sure nothing overlaps, disappears or forces sideways scrolling.
  3. Find the phone number in two secondsIf it takes longer than that from any page, the layout changes.
  4. Read the words out loudShort sentences and plain names for your services, so a first-time visitor understands what you do without a glossary.

A dining room, a menu and a reservation line

Restaurants show the problem most clearly. A menu posted as a photo of a printed page is unreadable on a phone and invisible to Google. Put the menu on the page as real text, list the hours for each day, say whether you take reservations and how, and put the number where a thumb can reach it. A couple planning dinner near Main Street or St. Armands Circle should be able to decide in under a minute.

The same goes for shops on Siesta Key or in Gulf Gate and service businesses down in Venice: say where you are in the words customers use, and say it near the top.

Lakewood Ranch and the younger households moving in

Sarasota is not only retirees. East of the city, straddling the Manatee and Sarasota county line, Lakewood Ranch has been the country's top-selling multigenerational master-planned community for eight straight years, according to RCLCO's rankings, and it was second overall in 2025 behind The Villages. In the first half of 2026 it recorded 1,064 new-home contracts. Wellen Park, in south Sarasota County near Venice, ranked third with 727.

Those buyers include young families who need pediatric dentists, vets, lawn care, tutors and pool service, and who search on a phone between other things. Good news: the same clear, large, simple page that works for a seventy-year-old works for a parent holding a toddler.

Google says local results depend on relevance, distance and prominence. A business that serves both the city and the new neighborhoods out east should say so on pages written about each place, which is what the ten city pages in Pro are for.

Sarasota website development, in plain terms

People use "design" and "development" loosely. For a dental office, a law practice or a home service company, what you need is the whole job: words written for your business, a layout that reads well, a contact form that emails every lead, the search setup Google reads, and hosting that keeps it running.

That is what we build. What we do not build is custom software, such as a patient portal or an online store. If you need one, we will tell you before you spend anything.

Free help close to home

The Florida SBDC at USF offers no-cost, face-to-face consulting to small businesses in Sarasota and Manatee counties. If you are still deciding what your business should say about itself, an hour there is a good start before you talk to any web designer.

Common questions

How much do web designers charge for a website in Sarasota?

Prices swing from a few hundred dollars for a do-it-yourself template to several thousand for an agency build, and many firms quote only after a meeting. Ours are printed and paid once: $497 for the 5-page Starter, $997 for Pro with ten pages plus ten city pages, and $1,997 for Agency. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep the AI agent. Our small business website cost guide walks through the wider market.

What should I ask Sarasota website design companies before hiring one?

Ask who writes the words, who owns the site and domain when it is done, what the monthly cost is after launch, and whether you can see your own site before paying. Also ask to see a page on a phone with the text size turned up. If the layout falls apart, older customers will see it fall apart too.

Do you offer Sarasota website development or just design?

We design, write and build the whole site, set up the contact form, titles, descriptions, sitemap and schema, and host it. That is what most local businesses mean by website development. Custom software, such as a patient portal or an online store, is not part of our packages, and we will say so up front if your project needs it.

Can you make my site easier for older customers to use?

Yes. That means body text large enough to read on a phone without zooming, strong contrast instead of light gray type, buttons labeled with words like "Call us" rather than icons alone, a phone number at the top of every page, and short pages that do not hide the important part behind menus.

Do you have an office in Sarasota?

No. Dominion Web Design Pro is Maurice Johnson, working from Big Sandy in East Texas. Everything happens by phone, email and preview links, and you approve each page before it goes live.

See your website before you pay for it

Give us your business name and what you do, and a demo site gets built for you to look at on your own phone. If you like it, pick a package. If you do not, you have spent nothing but the minute it took to look.
